defects: Drops the OrderTopology hypotheses on α and β (and TopologicalSpace α entirely) which are essential to the theorem: continuity only interacts with order structure this way when the topology is the order topology
Replaces LinearOrder α, LinearOrder β with SemilatticeSup α, SemilatticeSup β, a materially different (and non-comparable, not just weaker) order assumption
Uses sSup s and sSup (f '' s) but only assumes SemilatticeSup, which provides no SupSet instance, so the statement does not typecheck as written

Conclusion is stated as f (sSup s) = sSup (f '' s) for all s, using junk-value sSup semantics, instead of the gold's IsLUB-based LeftOrdContinuous, which only asserts the property for sets that actually have a supremum ('any set that has one') — these are not equivalent for sets lacking a supremum
Does not use/restate the actual Mathlib definition LeftOrdContinuous, producing a differently-shaped and not clearly equivalent proposition
